title: Library entry
description: A ready-made character, beast, or covenant — either extracted from a published book or written for this project to fill a gap in coverage.

facets.description: Structured, closed-vocabulary dimensions. These drive the filter UI; anything open-ended belongs in `tags` instead.

book.description: Slug of the source book. Redundant with `source` but denormalized so a single facet query answers 'a grog from Grogs'.

origin.description: published = extracted from licensed text; original = written for this project.

house.description: Hermetic House, for magi. Note the trademark conditions on House names in LICENSE.

role.description: What the entry is for at the table: turb, servant, artisan, antagonist, patron, mentor, quarry.

power.description: Rough tier, for filtering rather than balance. Beasts use Might where they have it.

region.description: Tribunal or geographic setting, where the entry is tied to one.

tags.description: Open vocabulary for everything the facets do not cover: 'crossbow', 'covenant-born', 'suspicious-of-magi', 'good-first-grog'. Lowercase, hyphenated. Tags are additive and never load-bearing for rules.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what this entry is and when a storyguide would reach for it. Written for this project, so `adaptation` is 'original' even when the stat block is verbatim.

block.description: The stat block, in the same shape the engine consumes for a built character. Absent for covenants, which use the covenant schema.

examples.name: Marsh Warden
examples.summary: A covenant-born watchman who knows the fen paths better than the roads. Written to fill a gap: the published grog templates are short on characters whose value is knowledge of the covenant's own terrain.
